newsitem.title: CHINA: Chinese yuan ends up at two-year high vs US dollar.
newsitem.headline: Chinese yuan ends up at two-year high vs US dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed up at a two-year high close of 8.2918 against the U.S. dollar in Shanghai on Friday, from Thursday's 8.2922 due to strong pro-yuan sentiment on the market, traders said.
The close was the highest since May 18, 1995 when the yuan ended at 8.2892.
The weighted average price on Thursday was 8.2921.

Dealers said pro-yuan sentiment dominated the market with China's foreign trade surplus surging in the first four months of this year, foreign investment continuing to flow into China and the central bank intervening less in the market recently.
The yuan opened unchanged at 8.2922 and fell to an intraday low of 8.2928 early in trading on profit-taking.
It then rose and moved mainly above the 8.2920 level for most of the session, hitting a high of 8.2914.
Trading was active early in the session but dull in late trading with most business done at 8.2920, traders said.
One dealer said that as today was the final trading day of the week, some traders were cautious.
"Some profit-taking emerged to depress the yuan early in the session," he said. "But strong pro-yuan sentiment brought forth heavy buying, pushing the yuan up."

Dealers said they expected the yuan to test the key 8.2900 resistance level early next week and and to move mainly in a range of 8.2900 to 8.2890 in the short term if the resistance level is breached.
The yuan on Friday closed up at 7.0978 from 7.1464 against 100 Japanese yen and up slightly at 1.0720 from 1.0724 against the Hong Kong dollar.
